headline: 18 contracts catalogued across Ethereum, Plume, and Solana; 7 Ethereum mainnet proxies/oracles, 3 Plume mainnet, 6 Solana mainnet, plus 1 Ethereum impl; upgradeable EIP-1967 transparent proxy architecture confirmed.

findings.text: D1: Etherscan search surfaced USTB Token Proxy at 0x43415eB6ff9DB7E26A15b704e7A3eDCe97d31C4e with name-tag 'Superstate: USTB Token' and confirmed EIP-1967 Transparent Proxy with impl SuperstateTokenV5_1 at 0x1f50a1ee0ec8275d0c83b7bb08896b4b47d6e8c4. Plume and Solana explorers not directly accessible; addresses sourced from docs instead. Direct Etherscan fetch failed (network); addresses confirmed via search snippets.

D2: Canonical deployed-contracts page found at https://docs.superstate.com/investors/smart-contracts. Lists 7 Ethereum mainnet addresses, 3 Plume mainnet addresses, 6+ Solana mainnet addresses with named roles. Deployed_contracts_doc set accordingly.

D3: docs.superstate.com lists 11 audits from 0xMacro (superstate-1 through superstate-11) and 1 from ChainSecurity (compound-suptb). No audit PDFs directly fetched this run due to tool call constraints; audit URLs recorded in protocol_metadata. D3 entries go to unknowns for address extraction.

D4: GitHub repo superstateinc/ustb confirmed with contract_deployment/ directory containing per-chain JSON files. README changelog lists commit SHAs for mainnet.json (dbd126e) and sepolia.json (d7e42b9). Direct fetch of contract_deployment/mainnet.json was blocked (GitHub domain not in allowlist for direct fetch). No SHA-pinned address artifact fetched this run.

D5: Three chains enumerated. Ethereum: 7 mainnet contracts + 1 impl. Plume Mainnet: 3 contracts (AllowlistV3 Proxy, USTB Token Proxy, USCC Token Proxy). Solana: 6 program/token addresses. Plume and Solana explorers not directly fetchable this run; all addresses sourced from docs.
D6: No factory pattern identified. USTB is a single-token issuance; AllowList is a singleton. No enumeration-view factory calls applicable.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: token (USTB proxy, USCC proxy), other (AllowlistV3 proxy), other (RedemptionIdle proxy), oracle (Continuous Price Oracle, Chainlink USTB/USCC oracles), other (Solana Allowlist, Burn Address, Pyth oracles). Superstate Admin Address referenced in docs as controlling minting/allowlist but its EOA/multisig address not surfaced from fetched sources.

D8: All EVM admin_addresses[] entries trace to the fetched docs.superstate.com/investors/smart-contracts page or the Etherscan search result snippet. Solana addresses are non-EVM and recorded in evidence only. The 'Superstate Admin Address' controlling minting/allowlist is referenced in docs but its actual address was not surfaced; recorded in unknowns.

rationale.verdict: Walked superstate.com, docs.superstate.com/investors/smart-contracts, github.com/superstateinc/ustb, and Etherscan search results. Catalogued 18 contract/program addresses across Ethereum (8), Plume (3), and Solana (6+burn address) from the official docs deployments page. Grade is unknown as this is a discovery slice.

protocol_metadata.about: Superstate's USTB is a tokenized share of the Superstate Short Duration US Government Securities Fund (renamed Invesco US Government Securities Fund), which invests in short-duration U.S. Treasury Bills targeting returns near the federal funds rate. Investors subscribe and redeem using USDC or USD, with shares issued as ERC-20 tokens on Ethereum and Plume or SPL Token-2022 tokens on Solana. All token transfers require both sender and receiver to be on Superstate's KYC-gated Allowlist, which only the Superstate Admin Address can modify. The protocol uses upgradeable EIP-1967 Transparent Proxy contracts on EVM chains and a novel SPL Token-2022 Allowlist program on Solana, with continuous NAV pricing powered by an on-chain oracle.
